messages:
incident-bot: 🚨 INCIDENT: High rate of container restarts in serving-eu-west-1 (GPU OOMs during prefill). Pager triggered for oncall. service: runtime-serving-prod, symptom: prefill OOM + CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY, impact: some long-context requests failing
sara_dev: seeing the same in Grafana - spike in OOMs starting ~10:04 UTC, error rate ~12% for that pool. dash: https://grafana.company/internal/d/RUNTIME/ooms?var=pool=eu-west-1
mike_oncall: i'm oncall. pinging infra. i'll grab logs and tail affected pods.
lee_infra: on it, pulling node metrics. nodes showing memory fragmentation and repeated nv_peer_mem errors, likely large prefill requests >100k tokens in a few sessions.
anya_sre: can we temporarily throttle prefill length or reject >X tokens per request? We have a hotfix we used before: set PREFILL_MAX_TOKENS and enable early-evict.
alice_support: heads up — two customers reported 500s in their dashboards. cust-alpha and cust-gamma. i've started drafting a customer note.
tim_sales: any ETA? customers asking if this is a platform issue. need language for AEs.
ops_manager: quick status update for customers: we're aware, mitigation in progress to limit extremely long prefill windows, no data loss. ETA 15-30m for initial mitigation.
sara_dev: log snippet from a restarted container:
```
2026-02-14T10:06:12Z runtime ERROR prefill_worker.cpp:234 OOM allocating 312469120 bytes (requested 312469120)
[  CUDA ] CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY: 0x7e at /workspace/runtime/cuda_utils.cu:412
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::bad_alloc'
container exiting with code 137
```
mike_oncall: thanks. i see repeated ``prefill_worker`` logs. suspect large context + continuous batching causing KV cache exhaustion. Plan: 1) set PREFILL_MAX_TOKENS=2048 for serving-eu-west-1 2) enable prefill-eviction flag 3) restart runtime daemonset on a rolling basis to pickup flag. i'll coordinate.
lee_infra: recommend also setting per-route soft-limits and returning 413 for requests > limit. we can do that quickly with a feature-flag rollback.
deploy-bot: config-change queued: user=mike_oncall action=set PREFILL_MAX_TOKENS=2048 --env=prod --pool=serving-eu-west-1 id=cfg-5982
mike_oncall: applying hotpatch now: `rctl set-config --pool serving-eu-west-1 --set PREFILL_MAX_TOKENS=2048 && rctl set-config --pool serving-eu-west-1 --set PREFILL_PREFETCH_EVICT=true`
lee_infra: once config applied i'll trigger controlled restarts: `kubectl rollout restart daemonset/serving-runtime -n prod --selector=pool=serving-eu-west-1` — doing it one AZ at a time
anya_sre: also flip batcher to strict batching=off for that pool to reduce peak mem during prefill, doing that in parallel.
alice_support: FYI sent initial customer notification to cust-alpha/cust-gamma: short note, investigating and applying temporary rate-limits.
mike_oncall: hotpatch applied. rolling restarts started (az1). monitoring logs and error rate.
lee_infra: az1 restarted, pod churn expected ~90s per pod. error spikes dropped by ~40% after PREFILL_MAX_TOKENS set.
deploy-bot: config-change applied: id=cfg-5982 status=success applied_by=mike_oncall ts=1767779022
ops_manager: drafting status update for status.redwood.ai — brief incident message + mitigation steps and expected follow-ups.
tim_sales: please include whether this affects SLA and if we will credit impacted customers.
anya_sre: preliminary root cause hypothesis: large-context prefill combined with continuous batching leads to transient KV cache growth that crosses per-GPU memory threshold. when allocation fails, runtime aborts the container. follow-up: add early-trim of prefill KV and better allocation checks.
sara_dev: monitoring metrics: error rate down to 3% from 12%, container restarts still occurring but much less frequent. cadence of restarts seems correlated with very long single-session prompts.
mike_oncall: i'm going to enable an emergency fallback to cold-model for requests over 8k tokens to avoid GPU OOMs while we build a longer term fix. executing: `rctl route set-fallback --pool serving-eu-west-1 --threshold 8000 --fallback=cpu-coldmodel`
lee_infra: confirmed fallback rule in place. logs show requests >8k being routed to cpu-coldmodel. those requests succeed but with higher latency, customers see 2-3x latency increase.
alice_support: updated customers: mitigation applied, some requests may be slower but successful. next update in 2 hours or when resolved.
ops_manager: we should schedule a postmortem tomorrow and notify infra/research/runtime teams. assign owners for follow-ups: model-eviction engineering, batcher improvements, and rate-limit UX.
mike_oncall: leaving note for next oncall: work done, continuing to monitor. will handoff at shift change. @anya_sre you're next on the rotation?
anya_sre: i can take the handoff, will keep an eye for residue restarts and drive the postmortem.
ops_manager: great. Incident status: mitigated -> partial; impact reduced, workaround in place. escalation: none at this time.
deploy-bot: incident-thread auto-update: severity=high, status=mitigated, incident_id=INC-2026-1023-01
alice_support: logging full list of affected tenants for billing/credit review: cust-alpha, cust-gamma, cust-delta (low volume requests), cust-theta (retry spikes).
anya_sre: adding temporary alert rule: alert if container_restarts_rate > 0.5% over 5m for pool=serving-eu-west-1.
sara_dev: logs look healthier. will keep dashboards on for next 6 hours.
mike_oncall: final note: major mitigations applied: PREFILL_MAX_TOKENS=2048, prefill-eviction enabled, strict batching off, emergency fallback to cpu-coldmodel for >8k tokens, rolling restarts. Postmortem owners assigned. Handoff complete. :white_check_mark:
